items.stem: For a rigid body in static equilibrium in a plane:

options.text: The sums of forces in two directions and of moments are all zero
options.rationale: Correct: plane equilibrium requires sum Fx = sum Fy = sum M = 0.

options.text: Only the sum of vertical forces must be zero
options.rationale: Horizontal forces and moments must also balance.

options.text: The body must be moving at constant velocity
Moments can be ignored if forces balance
options.rationale: Moment balance is an independent requirement.

items.explanation: Correct: plane equilibrium requires sum Fx = sum Fy = sum M = 0.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO assumptions underlie ideal truss analysis? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Members carry only axial force (tension or compression)
options.rationale: Correct: ideal truss members are two-force members.

options.text: Loads are applied only at the joints
options.rationale: Correct: joint loading keeps members axial.

options.text: Joints are rigid and transmit bending moments
options.rationale: Ideal truss joints are pinned, carrying no moment.

options.text: Every member must be in tension
options.rationale: Members may be in tension or compression.

items.explanation: Correct: ideal truss members are two-force members.

items.stem: The moment of a force about a point equals:

options.text: The force multiplied by the perpendicular distance to its line of action
options.rationale: Correct: moment = force x perpendicular (moment) arm.

options.text: The force multiplied by the time applied
The force divided by the distance
options.rationale: Moment is a product, not a quotient.

options.text: The force regardless of where it acts
options.rationale: Position relative to the point is essential.

items.explanation: Correct: moment = force x perpendicular (moment) arm.
